battle.name: 亞述征服亞蘭
battle.theater: 敘利亞北部卡爾卡爾河畔
battle.brief: 前853年（低年表作前854年），亞述王沙拉曼納三世渡幼發拉底河深入阿馬爾，在奧龍特斯河畔卡爾卡爾與大馬士革王哈達德召集的十二國聯軍遭遇。聯軍出動一千一百輛戰車與十二萬步兵，亞述以鐵矛、鐵箭配車騎兩翼迂迴破陣。埃及法老奧爾松一世派兵助聯軍，其埃及式長矛與圓盾步兵未能扭轉局勢。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 亞述征服亞蘭發生在亞述中王國西征最盛的年代，戰場上對陣的是亞述王國與以大馬士革為核心的亞蘭聯軍，埃及第二十一王朝則是聯軍背後的遠方支持者。亞述一方由沙拉曼納三世直接統帥，國王本人即是全軍最高指揮；中亞述的省級總督與城邑守將各自管轄駐防兵員與徵發的人力，野戰部隊則由王室近衛、王家騎兵與圖爾塔努一級的戰場指揮官率領。亞述此時已有常備的騎兵與車隊，兵源一部分是各省徵召的義勇民兵，一部分是亞述以外的僱傭兵，軍隊的核心則是握有鐵矛、鐵箭與鐵鎧的王室工匠所供應的裝備。聯軍一方並非單一國家，而是十一至十二個城邦與部落政體組成的鬆散聯盟，核心是大馬士革王哈達德，此外有卡爾卡爾王金迪布、索巴王、卡爾基米什王、阿勒頗王蘇姆拉比、撒馬爾王薩姆西穆魯納、亞捫王等，各自率本國的戰車、騎兵與步兵，沒有統一最高指揮，只靠大馬士革的盟主地位維持協同。聯軍的戰力以車兵為重心，卡爾卡爾一地即出動一千輛戰車與一千騎兵，可見亞蘭諸城在亞述壓力之下仍保有可觀的鍛造與徵召能力。埃及方面，二十一王朝法老奧爾松一世在位第二十一年向聯軍派出小股援軍，這是埃及軍隊在敘利亞與巴勒斯坦有文字記載的最早一次出現。兩套指揮系統的差異正是此役的關鍵：亞述能把數萬人編為一個作戰整體並同時指揮兩翼，聯軍兵力總數雖大，卻只能在多個指揮中心之間靠事前商定的方式配合，戰局一變便難以收束。
countriesEn: The Assyrian conquest of Aram took place at the height of the Middle Assyrian westward campaigns, and the battle array was between the kingdom of Assyria and an Aramean coalition centred on Damascus, with the Twenty-First Dynasty of Egypt as a distant supporter standing behind the coalition. The Assyrian side was commanded directly by Shalmaneser III, the king himself being the supreme commander of the whole army; in the Middle Assyrian system provincial governors and city commandants each held their own garrisons and their own levy of labour, while the field army was led by the royal guard, the royal cavalry and field commanders of the rank of turtanu. Assyria by this time possessed a standing cavalry and a chariot corps; part of the manpower came from levies raised in the provinces and part from mercenaries recruited from beyond Assyria, and the core of the force was equipped from the workshops of the royal armourers, who supplied iron spearheads, iron arrowheads and iron armour. The opposing camp was not a single state but a loose league of eleven or twelve city-states and tribal polities, its core being Hadad, king of Damascus, alongside Gindibu of Qarqar, the king of Soba, the king of Carchemish, Sumurabi of Aleppo, Samsimuruna of Sam'al and the Ammonite king, each bringing the chariots, cavalry and infantry of his own city, with no single supreme command, cohesion resting only on the hegemonic position of Damascus. The weight of the coalition lay on its chariot arm, since Qarqar alone put a thousand chariots and a thousand cavalry into the field, which shows that the Aramean cities retained considerable capacity in smithing and in levy even under Assyrian pressure. Egypt entered through Pharaoh Osorkon I of the Twenty-First Dynasty, who in the twenty-first year of his reign sent a small contingent to the coalition; this is the earliest documented appearance of an Egyptian army in Syria and Palestine. The difference between the two command systems is the key to the engagement: Assyria could marshal tens of thousands of men as a single body of combat and direct both wings at once, whereas the coalition, though larger in total, could only coordinate among several centres of command, and once the battle turned it could not be brought back together.
people: 留下姓名的有兩類：亞述方面的國王與戰場指揮官，亞蘭方面的諸王與其統兵者。亞述王沙拉曼納三世約前858年至前824年在位，父王阿達德尼拉里三世已三度西征直抵地中海；沙拉曼納三世以王儲身份隨父作戰，前858年首次抵地中海，前856年攻下北方重鎮阿爾帕德並擒獲撒馬爾王阿蘇爾，前853年再率大軍深入阿馬爾，前841年的黑色方尖碑上又刻下以色列王耶戶朝貢的圖像，這位國王的所得與所失都留下可核對的痕跡。聯軍的核心是大馬士革王哈達德，即聖經所稱的便哈達，舊約記載他與以色列王亞哈結盟、率大軍圍攻撒馬利亞，後來因以色列先知以利沙治愈亞捫元帥拿曼之事而改奉真主（此說見於約瑟夫斯《古史》），希伯來史家通常把他列為便哈達三世。亞哈是以色列王，約前903年至前862年在位，他與大馬士革的同盟兼有婚姻與文書兩重憑據；聯盟在卡爾卡爾崩潰數年後，他於前853年或前852年陣亡於拉末基列的戰役，耶戶隨即承位，並在前841年轉向亞述稱臣。聯軍中最具軍力的是卡爾卡爾王金迪布，亞述碑文記他獨力出動一千輛戰車與一千騎兵，在整個聯軍中佔比極高。與會的還有索巴王、卡爾基米什王、阿勒頗王蘇姆拉比、撒馬爾王薩姆西穆魯納與亞捫王等；亞述的卡爾卡爾銘文保存了十二位國王的名單，但其中數位已殘損難辨。埃及方面留下的不是姓名而是一條編年：奧爾松一世在位第二十一年向大馬士革方向派兵。除此之外還有大量以群體出現的人：亞述的弓手、投石手與持鐵矛的步兵，亞蘭諸城的車夫與重裝步兵，以及在最後一刻決定戰局、卻沒有留下姓名的基層軍人。
peopleEn: Two kinds of names survive: kings and battlefield commanders from Assyria, and the rulers and war leaders of Aram. The Assyrian king Shalmaneser III reigned from about 858 to 824 BC, and his father Adad-nirari III had already marched west three times to the Mediterranean. Shalmaneser III campaigned in his father's army as crown prince, first reaching the Mediterranean in 858 BC, taking the northern stronghold of Arpad in 856 BC and capturing the king of Sam'al, Ausur, and leading a large army deep into the Amurru in 853 BC; in 841 BC the Black Obelisk carried the image of the king of Israel, Jehu, bringing tribute to him, and this king's gains and losses both left checkable traces. The core of the coalition was Hadad, king of Damascus, the Aramean king called Ben-Hadad in the Bible, who is recorded in the Hebrew Bible as allied with the king of Israel, Ahab, leading a great army against Samaria and later, moved by the story of the prophet Elisha cleansing the Aramean commander Naaman, professing faith, a tradition preserved by Josephus; Hebrew historians usually number him as Ben-Hadad III. Ahab was king of Israel, roughly 903 to 862 BC, and his alliance with Damascus rested on both marriage and document, and it was this alliance that stood at the centre of the coalition before it broke. Ahab died at the battle of Ramoth Gilead in 853 or 852 BC, a few years after Qarqar, and Jehu succeeded him and turned to submission to Assyria in about 841 BC. The strongest single contribution to the coalition came from Gindibu, king of Qarqar, whom the Assyrian inscription records as fielding a thousand chariots and a thousand cavalry, a very large share of the whole force. Also present were the king of Soba, the king of Carchemish, Sumurabi of Aleppo, Samsimuruna of Sam'al and the Ammonite king; the Assyrian inscription of Qarqar preserves the list of twelve kings, though several names are broken and hard to read. What Egypt left behind was not a name but a date: Osorkon I in the twenty-first year of his reign sent troops in the direction of Damascus. Alongside these there are the people who appear only in groups: the Assyrian archers, slingers and iron-spearmen, the charioteers and heavy infantry of the Aramean cities, and the nameless rank and file whose action in the last moments decided the outcome.
kits: 卡面上的埃及長矛是早王朝時期的直刃長矛，銅或青銅矛頭以榫口或縛紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩，埃及人先以它守城垣，後來以它收復失地。到了公元前十至前九世紀，埃及式重裝矛兵陣早已瓦解，這件兵器在亞蘭戰場上出現的方式也隨之改變，它更多是埃及式裝備的一個標記，而不是某支埃及軍隊的實物裝備。亞述一方在此時已完成從青銅轉向鐵的關鍵變化，長矛的矛頭改為鐵製，箭鏃大量用鐵，鎧甲以鐵片綴成，甲胄與武器由王室的中央工坊與各省的徵集共同供應；亞述兵在野外所用的長矛比埃及矛短而厚實，屬直刺型，適合密集隊形中的正面推刺，這正是亞述步兵與亞蘭重裝步兵在兵種上的分野。聯軍的裝備以車兵為骨架：亞蘭式雙輪輕戰車，車身窄而無甲，一匹或兩匹馬拉動，一千輛同時投入作戰的規模在歐亞大陸前所未見；步兵以弓箭手與持矛重裝兵為主，使用複合弓，箭鏃可以是銅、鐵或骨，配圓形木胎蒙皮盾，另有短劍與斧。卡爾卡爾銘文提到聯軍裝備鐵製鎧甲與鐵的武器，對此有兩種讀法：或指亞蘭人靠鐵鎧與鐵兵抵擋亞述，或指亞述的鐵兵破開了聯軍的防線；無論取哪一說，這場會戰都常被當作鐵兵器第一次大規模用於會戰的證據。攻城與運輸方面，聯軍倚靠城牆與地形，亞述則以車隊、騾馬與牛車運糧，渡過幼發拉底與奧龍特斯之後全靠就地徵發，這條補給線的長度是它每次西征最吃力的地方。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a straight-bladed weapon of the Early Dynastic period, its copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder, used by the Egyptians first to hold city walls and later to win back lost ground. By the tenth and ninth centuries BC the Egyptian heavy spear line had long since dissolved, and the way this weapon appeared on the Aramean battlefield had changed with it: it was now more a marker of Egyptian-style equipment than the actual kit of any Egyptian army. The Assyrian side had by this time completed the decisive transition from bronze to iron, the long spearhead becoming iron, iron used in bulk for arrowheads, and armour assembled from iron plates, with arms and armour supplied jointly by the central workshops of the royal armourers and by provincial levies; the spears carried by Assyrian infantry in the field were shorter and heavier than the Egyptian ones, of the thrusting kind suited to pushing forward in close order, and this is the divide between the Assyrian foot and the Aramean heavy infantry. The coalition equipment rested on a framework of chariots: light two-wheeled Aramean chariots, narrow and without armour, drawn by one or two horses, with a thousand vehicles committed to a single battle, a scale without precedent anywhere in Eurasia; the infantry consisted mainly of archers and spearmen, using composite bows with arrowheads of copper, iron or bone, round wooden shields covered with hide, and short swords and axes. The Qarqar inscription refers to the coalition's iron armour and iron weapons, and two readings of this are possible: either that the Arameans met Assyria with iron armour and iron arms, or that the Assyrian iron weapons broke open the coalition's line; on either reading, the engagement is often treated as evidence of the first large-scale use of iron weapons in a set-piece battle. As for siege and transport, the coalition relied on walls and on terrain, while Assyria moved grain on wagons, mules and ox carts and depended entirely on requisition once it had crossed the Euphrates and the Orontes; the length of that supply line was the most expensive part of every western campaign.
tactics: 亞述在前九世紀形成的野戰打法，到沙拉曼納三世這一代已趨成熟：全軍排成寬大的新月形，兩翼是車隊與騎兵，中間留出供步卒與弓箭手使用的正面，箭雨的作用不是消滅敵人，而是限制敵人展開，迫使其在不利的地形上接戰；敵陣一旦被牽制，兩翼即向內合圍包抄，把正面壓力與側翼威脅疊在一起。卡爾卡爾的地理完全適合這種打法，奧龍特斯河谷是兩山之間狹長的走廊，聯軍要守住渡口便無法展開，亞述則可利用河谷的縱深把車隊與騎兵送到聯軍兩側。聯軍的部署以卡爾卡爾王金迪布的一千輛戰車與一千騎兵作為中軍骨幹，兩翼以步兵與弓箭手延展，車兵集中衝擊亞述正面；亞述的應對是先以弓箭手與持鐵矛的步兵頂住車陣衝擊，再讓兩翼在聯軍側後完成包抄。結果是聯軍的車兵退不回來，步兵無法收縮，整條戰線在縱深不足的情況下崩潰，亞述碑文說聯軍的戰士沒有守住陣地而四散奔逃。作戰季節方面，亞述在西部地區的出征通常自依雅魯月展開，到提斯里月收束，本目錄所填的月份按此戰役季節推算，並非文獻記載；車隊與騎兵的補給依賴幼發拉底中游的城市與軍需站，渡河之後靠當地徵發與徵用牲畜維持，因此這支部隊的作戰半徑受到嚴格限制，最遠不能越過阿馬爾的海岸。防禦方面，聯軍倚靠地形與數量上的縱深而非縱深工事，這也解釋了它為何在正面被牽制住之後，會在短時間內全面瓦解。
tacticsEn: The way Assyria fought in the field had already matured by the generation of Shalmaneser III: the army was drawn up in a broad crescent, chariots and cavalry on the wings, the centre left for the foot and the archers, and the function of the arrow shower was not to destroy the enemy but to deny him room to deploy, forcing him to accept contact on ground of the Assyrians' choosing; once the enemy was held in place, the wings would close inward and encircle, stacking frontal pressure against flank threat. The ground at Qarqar suited this method perfectly. The Orontes valley is a narrow corridor between two mountain ranges, so a coalition that meant to hold the ford could not deploy, while Assyria could use the length of the valley to bring its chariots and cavalry around onto the coalition's flanks. The coalition arrayed Gindibu of Qarqar with his thousand chariots and thousand cavalry as the skeleton of the centre, with infantry and archers extended along the wings, the chariots massed to strike the Assyrian front; the Assyrian answer was to absorb the impact of the charge with archers and iron-spearmen, and then to close the wings behind the coalition's flank and complete the encirclement. The result was that the coalition chariots could not withdraw and the infantry could not compress, and the whole line collapsed for want of depth, the Assyrian inscription saying that the warriors of the coalition did not hold their ground but fled in every direction. As for the campaigning season, the Assyrian expeditions to the west usually opened in the month of Ayyaru and were closed out in Tishri, and the month entered in this record follows that campaigning season rather than any statement in the sources. Supply for chariots and horses rested on the cities and relay stations of the middle Euphrates, and once across the river everything was maintained by requisition and by animals taken from the country, so the radius of this army was strictly limited and could not at the furthest reach the coast of the Amurru. On the defensive side, the coalition relied on terrain and on numerical depth rather than on works of fortification, which also explains why, once its front was held, it came apart completely within a short time.
data: 可核對的數字主要有三組。第一組是時間：本目錄採用的前854年對應亞述年表中的低年表，在通行的中年表裡這場會戰被定於前853年，兩者相差一年，是學界對沙拉曼納三世即位年代之爭所造成，而不是兩場不同的戰役。第二組是亞述碑文自報的聯軍兵力，步兵十二萬、騎兵一萬、戰車一千一百輛，其中卡爾卡爾王金迪布一人即出一千輛戰車與一千騎兵；但同一份文獻在另一段提到以色列王以利亞胡時，仍寫出戰車一千輛、騎兵一萬、步兵十萬這組幾乎相同的數字，可見這些數目帶有明顯的修辭成分，不宜當作實數看待，比較穩妥的說法是聯軍總兵力在數萬之數、戰車以千計，而亞述方面的具體人數碑文未載。第三組是距離與行程：亞述首都尼尼微到卡爾卡爾直線約七百公里，實際行程因需迂迴幼發拉底與山區隘口而更長；大馬士革到卡爾卡爾約二百五十公里；卡爾卡爾渡口距幼發拉底最近渡點約一百公里，而亞述西征軍通常要在同一個征戰季內走完往返，時間極緊。另有兩個年代錨點可用：以色列王耶戶向亞述朝貢記載於前841年，埃及法老奧爾松一世在位第二十一年亦有編年，兩者共同把這場會戰夾在前858年與前841年之間。戰場位置本身也經過考定：卡爾卡爾一般認為在今敘利亞西北部奧龍特斯河上游的卡爾卡爾村一帶。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three groups. The first is chronology: the 854 BC used in this record corresponds to the low chronology of the Assyrian king list, while the widely used middle chronology dates this engagement to 853 BC; the one-year difference is the product of scholarly disagreement over the accession year of Shalmaneser III and not of two separate battles. The second group is the coalition strength reported by the Assyrian inscription: one hundred and twenty thousand foot, ten thousand horses and one thousand one hundred chariots, of which Gindibu of Qarqar alone supplied a thousand chariots and a thousand cavalry. Yet the same text, in another passage concerning the king of Israel, Ish-paliyahu, again gives a thousand chariots, ten thousand horses and a hundred thousand foot, figures almost identical, which shows that these numbers carry a strong rhetorical element and should not be taken literally. The safer statement is that the coalition numbered tens of thousands of men with chariots in the thousands, while the Assyrian side is given no figure at all. The third group is distance and marching: about seven hundred kilometres in a straight line from the Assyrian capital of Nineveh to Qarqar, and considerably longer in practice because the route had to bend around the Euphrates and the mountain passes; about two hundred and fifty kilometres from Damascus to Qarqar; and about a hundred kilometres from the ford at Qarqar to the nearest crossing of the Euphrates, while the Assyrian army had normally to cover the outward and return march inside a single campaigning season, leaving very little room. Two further chronological anchors are available: the tribute of Jehu of Israel to Assyria is recorded for 841 BC, and there is an annal for the twenty-first year of the reign of the Egyptian Pharaoh Osorkon I, and together they bracket this engagement between 858 and 841 BC. The site of the battle is itself established: Qarqar is generally identified with the village of that name on the upper Orontes in north-western Syria.
cause: 直接導火線是亞述對阿馬爾的推進。前十世紀末，赫梯帝國崩解、埃及第二十王朝在西奈與迦南的統治收縮之後，亞蘭諸城一度取得相對的自主，但亞述並不打算接受這種局面。阿達德尼拉里三世已把勢力推至幼發拉底上游與地中海一帶，其子沙拉曼納三世即位後面對的是實際上各自為政的阿馬爾諸國：北方重鎮阿爾帕德由當地統治者控制，撒馬爾一度脫離亞述，敘利亞南部與北部城市各自進貢卻不聽節制。亞述的戰略目標很清楚，就是恢復對這條走廊的控制，同時切斷大馬士革的聯盟網與南方商路。聯軍之所以能集結到空前規模，也是因為目標相同：大馬士革王哈達德要在亞述進入阿馬爾之前先把它擋在奧龍特斯河一線，若能在河谷得手，便能保住亞蘭諸國的獨立；以色列王亞哈與大馬士革的同盟則有婚姻與盟約作保，一同加入聯軍。埃及的介入出於維持自己那份已經縮水的西亞利益：二十一王朝的奧爾松一世向聯軍派兵，並且在加沙一線維持對腓尼基城邦的影響。三方各有各的理由，衝突在亞述西進的推力與亞蘭聯軍的守土意願之間成形；具體是哪一次越界、哪一支巡邏隊引發接觸，文獻沒有留下記載，合理的推測是亞述西進的先鋒與聯軍的前哨在渡口一帶迎面相撞，隨即演成雙方傾全力的會戰。
causeEn: The immediate occasion was the Assyrian advance into the Amurru. After the collapse of the Hittite empire and the contraction of Egyptian rule over Sinai and Canaan at the end of the tenth century BC, the Aramean cities enjoyed a measure of independence, but Assyria was not prepared to accept that state of affairs. Adad-nirari III had already pushed his power to the upper Euphrates and to the Mediterranean, and his son Shalmaneser III on accession found the Amurru states in fact governing themselves: the northern stronghold of Arpad was in the hands of a local ruler, Sam'al had for a time slipped out of Assyrian control, and the cities of northern and southern Syria paid tribute while refusing to take orders. The Assyrian strategic aim was plain: to restore control of that corridor and at the same time cut the Damascus alliance and the southern trade routes. The coalition was able to assemble on an unprecedented scale because it shared that aim. Hadad of Damascus wanted to hold Assyria on the line of the Orontes before it entered the Amurru, for a victory in the valley would preserve the independence of the Aramean states; the alliance of the king of Israel, Ahab, with Damascus was secured by marriage and by treaty, and so Israel joined the coalition. Egypt entered to defend the shrunken share of its western Asian interests: Osorkon I of the Twenty-First Dynasty sent troops to the coalition and maintained his influence over the Phoenician city states on the Gaza line. Each of the three parties had its own reason, and the clash took shape between the Assyrian push to the west and the Aramean coalition's determination to hold its ground. Which specific crossing or which scouting party first made contact is not recorded, and the most reasonable reconstruction is that a forward detachment of the Assyrian advance and an outlying party of the coalition met face to face near the ford, and that the encounter grew at once into a battle in which both sides committed everything.
impact: 這場會戰的短期後果是亞蘭聯盟的崩解與亞述西進的加速。聯軍各王失去大批車兵與重裝步兵，許多城邦隨後淪為亞述的進貢國；大馬士革雖然仍能維持表面上的強盛，前853年之後卻失去了對北部亞蘭的盟主地位，直到前838至前837年亞述再度大舉西征、攻破大馬士革與撒馬爾，才真正被壓到附庸的境地。以色列則以另一種方式度過這一關：亞哈陣亡，耶戶即位後在約前841年向亞述朝貢，繳納的貢品包括銀、金、金碗、尖底金瓶、金杯、金桶、錫、王杖與長矛，亞述人沒有摧毀以色列的國家結構，只要求它留在體系之內，這也是亞述宗主附庸體系最早的成形樣本之一。長期看，這一戰把黎凡特從多國並存的平衡推入亞述主導的秩序，前八世紀亞述新王朝能一路打到埃及，前提正是前九世紀已經把這些城邦編入進貢網絡與省級行政之中；亞述同時把被征服地區的部分人口與戰俘徙置到省境，作為壓制當地與補充人力的手段。另一層影響屬於技術史：亞述在鐵器上的儲備與供應在此時已成形，會戰中大量使用鐵矛、鐵箭與鐵鎧被記錄下來，隨後數個世紀安納托利亞與歐洲的鐵器技術傳播路徑，與此役之後亞述對西部資源的系統性抽取密切相關。對卡面上那件埃及長矛而言，這場戰爭的意義更為冷峻：亞蘭諸城的重裝步兵與埃及援軍所用的仍帶有新王國時代的痕跡，而亞述的鐵矛與更嚴整的隊形決定了勝負，此後黎凡特的步兵裝備逐步被亞述樣式取代，埃及式長矛從此退成遙遠的傳統象徵。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the battle was the breaking of the Aramean alliance and the quickening of the Assyrian advance. The kings of the coalition lost large numbers of charioteers and heavy infantry, and many of the city states became tributary to Assyria thereafter. Damascus could still keep up an appearance of strength, but after 853 BC it lost its position as hegemon of northern Aram, and it was not until the great Assyrian campaigns of 838 and 837 BC, when Damascus and Sam'al were stormed, that it was truly pressed down to the condition of a vassal. Israel passed through the crisis in a different way: Ahab was killed, and after his accession Jehu brought tribute to Assyria in about 841 BC, giving up silver, gold, a golden bowl, a golden vase with a pointed bottom, golden tumblers, golden buckets, tin, a staff for a king and spears; the Assyrians did not destroy the structure of the Israelite state but required only that it remain within the system, and this is one of the earliest working models of the Assyrian overlord-and-vassal arrangement. In the long run the battle pushed the Levant out of a balance of many powers and into an order dominated by Assyria, and the fact that the Assyrian dynasty of the eighth century could march all the way to Egypt depended precisely on the fact that in the ninth century these city states had already been drawn into the network of tribute and the provincial administration; at the same time Assyria resettled part of the population and the prisoners of the conquered districts inside the provinces, as a means of control and of adding to the manpower. A second layer of impact belongs to the history of technology: the store and supply of iron in Assyria had by now taken shape, and the large-scale use of iron spears, iron arrows and iron armour in the battle was written down, and the spread of iron technology through Anatolia and Europe in the centuries that followed is closely tied to the systematic extraction of western resources by Assyria after this war. For the Egyptian spear on the card the meaning of the war is colder still: the heavy infantry of the Aramean cities and the Egyptian auxiliaries still bore the marks of the New Kingdom, while the iron spears and the tighter formations of Assyria decided the issue; the infantry equipment of the Levant was thereafter gradually replaced by Assyrian models, and the Egyptian spear receded into a distant traditional emblem.
result: 結果是亞述完勝，但勝利的方式值得細說。亞述碑文記載聯軍的國王們沒有守住陣地，大批戰車、馬匹與裝備被奪取，亞述軍把繳獲的馬、騾、驢與財貨運回幼發拉底；記載中特別提到聯軍一方的鐵鎧與鐵制武器落入亞述之手，這既可解讀為亞述的鐵兵破開了對方防線，也可解讀為亞述人繳獲並拆解了敵人的鐵鎧。以色列方面的損失在史料中只能推知而無法量化；舊約記載亞哈在迦密山屠殺四百五十名巴力先知，隨後在拉末基列的戰役中陣亡，屍首運回撒馬利亞安葬，耶戶隨即被擁立，而與亞述交涉的正是這個新王朝。前841年的黑色方尖碑把新的局面固定了下來：以色列作為亞述的附庸留在原地，亞述不再急著毀滅它，而是要求它定期進貢並提供人手。放到更長的尺度上，卡爾卡爾是亞述由中王國走向新亞述帝國的轉折點之一：聯軍的規模雖大卻缺乏統一指揮，亞述的規模雖小卻能把不同兵種合成為一個整體，這一對比在此役之後越來越多地得到證明；亞述由此取得西部的主動權，並在往後數十年內逐步拆解亞蘭的聯盟結構，最終把阿馬爾變成由省級總督直接管治的行省。
resultEn: The result was a complete Assyrian victory, but the manner of it deserves attention. The Assyrian inscription records that the kings of the coalition did not hold their ground, that large numbers of chariots, horses and equipment were taken, and that the Assyrian army carried off the horses, mules, donkeys and treasure they had captured back to the Euphrates; the text singles out the iron armour and the iron weapons of the coalition falling into Assyrian hands, which can be read either as the Assyrian iron weapons breaking the opposing line or as Assyrians stripping and breaking up the enemy's iron armour. The Israeli losses can be inferred from the sources but not quantified; the Hebrew Bible records that Ahab slew the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal at Mount Carmel, and that he then died at the battle of Ramoth Gilead, his body being brought back to Samaria for burial, with Jehu raised to the throne, and it was with this new dynasty that the approach to Assyria was made. The Black Obelisk of 841 BC fixed the new situation: Israel remained in place as a vassal of Assyria, which no longer needed to destroy it but required it to pay tribute at intervals and to provide men. On a longer scale, Qarqar was one of the turning points on the road from the Middle Assyrian kingdom to the Neo-Assyrian empire. The coalition was large but lacked a unified command; the Assyrian force was smaller but could fuse different arms into a single body, and this contrast was increasingly demonstrated after the battle. Assyria gained the initiative in the west, dismantled the Aramean alliance structure over the following decades, and in the end turned the Amurru into provinces governed directly by Assyrian governors.
